name: Town Centre (Mosi-oa-Tunya Road)
description: The compact core strung along Mosi-oa-Tunya Road, lined with shops, banks, markets, eateries, and faded colonial-era buildings plus the Livingstone Museum. It is the most practical base for errands, transport links, and everyday life close to amenities.
bestFor: Nomads wanting walkable amenities, banks, markets, and easy transport connections
pros: Central and walkable to shops and services
cons: Basic internet and occasional power cuts

name: Riverfront and Lodges (toward the Zambezi)
tagline: Scenic river lodges near the falls
description: The stretch running from town toward the Zambezi and Victoria Falls, home to riverfront lodges, sunset-cruise jetties, and quieter terraces. It is the most beautiful and restful area, though pricing skews higher and it sits a little apart from town errands.
bestFor: Nature lovers and lighter-workload nomads wanting river views and calm surroundings
pros: Better lodge Wi-Fi and quiet terraces
Close to cruises and the falls

name: Highlands (residential suburbs)
description: A settled residential suburb of houses and small compounds away from the tourist bustle, where longer-stay renters find quieter streets and a more local, everyday rhythm. It offers space and calm, though you will depend on transport into the centre.
bestFor: Longer-stay nomads seeking quiet residential rentals and an authentic local pace

name: Victoria Falls Entrance and Border
description: The southern zone near the Victoria Falls entrance, the Zambezi bridge, and the Zimbabwe border, packed with adventure operators, backpacker lodges, and the bungee bridge. It is the liveliest, most traveller-focused pocket, ideal for activities and easy cross-border day trips.
bestFor: Adventure seekers wanting the falls, bungee, rafting, and Zimbabwe day trips
pros: Walking distance to the falls and activities
